title: 1977 AHSME Problem 9
statement: In the adjoining figure \(\angle E=40^\circ\) and arc \(AB,\) arc \(BC\) and arc \(CD\) all have equal length. Find the measure of \(\angle ACD.\)

solutions.text:
Let each of arcs \(AB,\) \(BC,\) \(CD\) measure \(x^\circ\) and let arc \(AD\) measure \(y^\circ.\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} 3x+y&=360,\\ \frac{x-y}{2}&=40. \end{aligned} \] Solving gives \(y=30.\) The inscribed angle \(\angle ACD\) subtends arc \(AD,\) so it measures \(\frac{y}{2}=15^\circ.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Assign one variable to each of the three equal arcs and another to arc \(AD\)
Use both the full-circle arc sum and the external-secant angle theorem at \(E\)
